contract.name: Table Read UI contract
contract.purpose: The complete list of what exists in the Table Read macOS app today. A redesign may restyle and rearrange these things. It may not add, remove, rename or change what they do.
contract.howToRead: Every 'label' value is the exact text shown in the app. Text in {braces} is filled in at runtime, e.g. '{n} selected' shows as '3 selected'. 'help' is the hover tooltip. 'visibleWhen' and 'enabledWhen' are conditions that must be kept.
decisions: 2026-10-07: One window only. Settings, Onboarding, Report a Bug, Update Available and New Project are sheets or panels inside the main window; there are no separate windows.
2026-10-07: The app is being rebuilt in Flutter (macOS first). Labels and behavior in this file still bind the rebuild.
2026-10-07: Palette is 'blue leads' (azure blue for actions, highlighter yellow for the play button and your own lines). See the design notes in design/claude-design-1a-v2/.
2026-10-07: In the Archived view, the filter, view-mode and sort controls are hidden (they do nothing there).
2026-10-07: The Parser Corrections footer must keep the warning that contributed corrections are publicly visible on GitHub.
2026-10-11: Line rows no longer show a speaker color dot or a line-type symbol (“ ¶ +) in the gutter; the colored name tag carries the speaker. Two-voice rows drop the dot beside each name too.
2026-10-11: Line checkboxes are hidden until the row is hovered, checked, or a selection is active in that scene.
2026-10-11: Color roles: blue is the main color (primary buttons, play button, progress, selection, playing line); highlighter yellow is the accent (your own lines in Rehearse, brand mark).
2026-10-11: New setting (requested): Settings → General → Script Display → 'Character highlight colors', with On/Off previews. Off = neutral gray name tags everywhere.
2026-10-11: 'Edited' / 'Re-Render Edited Scenes' now compares each scene's edits with what was rendered; undoing or reverting an edit clears it.
2026-10-11: The side panel is gone. The workspace is: header (back, title, tool palette: Cast, Render, search) → script area → playback bar at the bottom. Cast and Render are sheets.
2026-10-11: The app options (Update Available, BETA, Report a Bug, Settings) are pinned to the top-right corner of the window on every screen.
2026-10-11: Parsing shows a determinate progress bar with a message ('Reading page 4 of 120'), not a spinner.
2026-10-11: After a new script is parsed, the Cast sheet opens once by itself; 'Done' confirms the cast. It reopens from Cast in the header (⌘K).

2026-10-11: Render opens the Render sheet (choose scenes, then 'Render N Scenes'). Edited scenes are preselected. Progress shows on each scene bar (thin line when collapsed, bar in the heading when expanded) and in a status chip in the header.
2026-10-11: Scene cards no longer carry a render checkbox; choosing scenes happens only in the Render sheet.

2026-10-11: Rehearse is the playback bar at the bottom: scene picker, transport, scene timeline with character-colored segments, My Role (mute, block, stop before my lines), Loop (scene or selected lines), Speed.
2026-10-11: Click any line (or its Play pill) to play from it. Keyboard: Space play/pause, ←/→ line, ⌘←/⌘→ scene, ⌘F search.
2026-10-11: Click a speaker's name tag on a line to change the speaker.
2026-10-11: Search bar in the header finds text in the script with 'N of M' and previous/next; matching scenes show a count.
2026-10-11: Cast shows how many lines each character has and sorts by it (Narrator first).
2026-10-11: Voice and engine changes count as edits for 'Edited' / re-render.
2026-10-11: Each project remembers its expanded scenes, role, mute/block/stop, and speed.
2026-10-11: Script stats (scenes · characters · lines) are a footer under the last scene.
2026-10-11: The Log moved to Debug → Show Log (⌥⌘L), shown in a sheet. Bug reports attach the last 40 log lines.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Character highlight colors off = plain name text, no tag behind it. The playback timeline always keeps character colors.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Play and pause always scroll to the playing line, opening its scene (and the folded part past the first 30 lines) when needed.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Engine choices are equal-size cards with an icon each; no engine is labeled 'Recommended'.

2026-10-11 (round 2): Line actions (Play, Edit, Remove, Add line) float over the row's top-right corner on hover instead of taking a column; dialogue sits in a centered column. Narration rows have no Narrator tag.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Cast, Render and search sit in a toolbar under the title bar, on the left.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Clicking BETA opens Settings → About.
2026-10-11 (round 2): Report a Bug's button is 'Submit on GitHub'; the report opens on GitHub and is sent from there (a GitHub account is needed).

2026-10-11 (round 2): Projects: a click opens a project; the checkbox selects (clicks then add to the selection). Rename is in the selection bar (one selected), the right-click menu and the ⋯ button (Open, Rename…, Archive, Delete…).

mustNot: Add any screen, mode, tab, panel, button, menu item, setting, toggle or feature that is not listed in this file.
Remove or hide any element listed here (making it hover-only is fine if it is already hover-only; see 'mayChange').
Rename any navigation item, tab, button, menu item or field label. Use the exact 'label' strings.
Change what any control does, or add new options to a menu or picker.
Move a control to a different screen, tab, sheet or popover than the one it is listed under.
Merge or split screens, tabs or sheets. The workspace has no side panel: header (tool palette: Cast, Render, Search), script area, playback bar.
Show data the app does not have (see 'notInApp' and 'dataShapes'). No waveforms, durations, costs, avatars, ratings or progress figures beyond those listed.
Invent a workflow, onboarding step or empty state that refers to features not listed here.
mayChange: Visual style: color, type, spacing, radius, borders, shadows, materials, icons, illustration, light and dark themes.
Layout and arrangement of elements within their own screen, region, sheet or popover, including order and grouping.
Size and emphasis: which action looks primary, how big the play button is, how prominent a tag is.
How an existing control is revealed: hover-only controls may become always visible, or the reverse, if nothing becomes unreachable.
Motion and transitions, as long as Reduce Motion is respected.
Explanatory body copy (empty-state messages, footers, onboarding descriptions, tooltips) may be reworded for clarity if the meaning does not change. Control labels in 'label' fields stay exact.
Visual treatment of states that already exist: selected, hovered, playing, removed, corrected, low-confidence, rendered, edited, disabled, loading, error.
rules.ifUnsure: Leave it out. List the idea separately under 'Suggestions (not in the app)' in your reply instead of putting it in the design.

notInApp.note: These have been proposed or invented before. None of them exist. Do not draw them.
items: A 'Record' tab or mode, or any 'Prep / Record / Rehearse' mode switcher
A persistent or mini player bar outside the Rehearse tab
A listening library, albums, tracks or playlists
Memorization progress, 'off book' marks or scores (the 'Memorized' sort option exists but has no data behind it)
A cast table, seating chart or drag-a-voice-onto-a-character
A flagged-lines walkthrough or 'next flagged line' navigation
A recording booth, call sheet or 'on air' view of the render queue
Waveforms, scene durations or a scrubber/timeline
An OpenAI cost or time estimate anywhere in the current UI
A 'Parenthetical' line type in any picker (the Type picker has only Dialog and Narration)
Search, tags, folders or collections for projects
Export or share buttons for audio (files are saved to disk; there is no export UI)
Accounts, sign-in, cloud sync, collaboration or comments

glossary.Projects: The home screen (Project Gallery). Header text: 'Table Read' / 'Projects'.
glossary.Project Dashboard: The screen for one open project (the workspace): header with the tool palette, the script area, and the playback bar at the bottom.
glossary.Narrator: The voice that reads everything that is not dialogue. Displayed as 'Narrator'. Always listed first in cast and speaker lists.
glossary.Removed: A line marked as not voiced. It stays visible, struck through, and can be restored. Never deleted.
glossary.Simultaneous: Two voices speaking one line at the same time, shown side by side.

navigation.window: One main window. Shows either Projects or a Project Dashboard, never both. Everything else (Settings, sheets, popovers) opens inside it.
flows: Projects → New Project → New Project sheet → system PDF picker → workspace (parse progress bar, then the script) → Cast sheet opens once → Done
Workspace → back chevron → Projects (asks to confirm if a render is running)
Workspace → Render (⌘R) → Render sheet → Render N Scenes → progress on the scene bars and the header status chip (click it to reopen the Render sheet)
Workspace → click a line, or the playback bar → playback
Any screen → gear button or ⌘, → Settings sheet (inside the main window)
Any screen → Report a Bug button or ⇧⌘B → Report a Bug sheet
Update Available badge, Settings, or app menu → Update Available sheet
First launch, or Help → Table Read Help (⌘?) → Onboarding sheet

sharedBehaviors.speakerColor: Each character has one color, used for their name tag, chips, timeline segments and cast row everywhere. Colors are generated per script and can be turned off (Settings → General → Character highlight colors). The redesign may replace the palette but must keep one consistent color per character across all screens.
sharedBehaviors.undoRedo: Every script edit can be undone. ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z and the Undo/Redo pill. Up to 50 steps.
sharedBehaviors.nonDestructiveEdits: Removed lines stay visible (struck through, 45% opacity) with Restore available.
sharedBehaviors.lightDark: Must work in light mode, dark mode and increased contrast.
